name: mdforge
description: Transform VS Code into a Typora-like WYSIWYG Markdown editor with GitHub-style rendering, Mermaid diagrams and rich task lists.

commands.title: MDForge: Open Original Side in MDForge
MDForge: Open Modified Side in MDForge

mdforge.checkbox.enableInProgress.description: Enable the custom [~] 'in progress' state in the checkbox click cycle (empty -> in progress -> done).

mdforge.format.onSave.markdownDescription:
Reformat the document automatically on every save — exactly what the toolbar's **¶ Reformat** button does: collapse duplicate blank lines, put a blank line around headings and code fences, end the file with a single newline, and — when `#mdforge.format.paragraphs#` is `oneLine` — bring each paragraph back onto a single line.

Off (the default): the file is reformatted only when you ask for it, with the ¶ button or the **MDForge: Reformat document** command.

mdforge.format.blankLines.markdownDeprecationMessage: Renamed: use `#mdforge.format.onSave#` (a checkbox). This setting is still honoured, but will be removed.

enumDescriptions: Keep the source line breaks inside paragraphs exactly as they are (default).

Put each paragraph back on a single line when the document is reformatted (the toolbar's paragraph button, the 'Normalize blank lines' command, and format-on-save). Required for justified text to have any visible effect.
mdforge.format.paragraphs.markdownDescription:
Whether reformatting also unwraps paragraphs onto one line. `oneLine` is needed by `#mdforge.textAlign#` = `justify`: justification never stretches the last line of a block, and every *source* line is a block — so a hard-wrapped paragraph cannot be justified. Code, tables, quotes, headings and deliberate hard breaks (two trailing spaces, `\`, `
`) are never touched.

mdforge.lineNumbers.description: Show source line numbers in the gutter.

mdforge.quickDiff.markdownDescription: Mark the lines added, modified or deleted since the last commit in the left margin. Compares the editor's live text (including unsaved changes) against the staged version, falling back to `HEAD`. Needs the built-in Git extension; files outside a repository show nothing.

mdforge.revealSearchMatch.markdownDescription: When a note is opened while the Search view is showing its results, go to the first match in that note and mark the other matching lines (`F8` / `Shift+F8` walk them). VS Code does not tell a custom editor which result was clicked ([microsoft/vscode#289785](https://github.com/microsoft/vscode/issues/289785)), so MDForge recovers the positions from the Search view itself — the line is highlighted, not the word.

mdforge.pageWidth.description: Content width: 'comfortable' centers a readable column (GitHub-like), 'full' spans the viewport.

mdforge.mermaid.fitWidth.description: Scale Mermaid diagrams up to the full width of the text column (off: keep the diagram's natural size, centered).

mdforge.paste.appendSource.description: When pasting from a web page, append a '> <label> <url>' blockquote below the paste and place the caret on it (the source URL is auto-filled only if the clipboard carries one).

mdforge.paste.sourceLabel.description: Label used by mdforge.paste.appendSource before the URL.

mdforge.debug.pasteHtml.description: Debug: on paste, open the raw clipboard HTML/plain-text in a new tab (to inspect what a web page actually puts on the clipboard, e.g. math markup).

markdownEnumDescriptions: Paragraphs are justified. Display-only — no HTML is written to the Markdown.
mdforge.textAlign.markdownDescription: Text alignment for paragraphs in the editor view (viewer preference; not stored in the file). `justify` only shows on wrapped lines, so set `#mdforge.format.paragraphs#` to `oneLine` and reformat once (toolbar ¶) to unwrap hard-wrapped paragraphs.

mdforge.images.folder.description: Folder (relative to the note) where pasted/dropped/picked images are saved. Empty = next to the note.

mdforge.images.naming.markdownDescription: File name pattern for saved images. Tokens: `${noteName}` (note file name without extension), `${hash}` (content hash), `${originalName}` (original file name without extension). The default mirrors the vault convention `NoteName-<hash>.ext`.

mdforge.images.hashLength.description: Number of hex characters of the content MD5 hash used in the image file name.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Follow the VS Code theme (dark editor → dark diagrams).
MDForge 'blue': a light, cool blue — pale fills, soft steel-blue outlines, deep navy text.
MDForge 'blue-dark': the same blue inverted for a dark editor.
MDForge 'contrast': white fills, **thick black** outlines, near-black **bold** labels — survives a projector, a printout, a screenshot.
MDForge 'contrast-dark': the same thick, bold drawing inverted for a dark editor.
mdforge.mermaid.theme.markdownDescription: Theme used to render Mermaid diagrams. A named theme is used as-is; only `auto` follows the editor.
mdforge.mermaid.theme.description: Theme used to render Mermaid diagrams.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Ask before renaming a changed image so its `<hash>` matches the new content.
Rename automatically (and update the link) when a changed image's content hash drifts.
Never rename on change (the `<hash>` in the file name may become stale).
mdforge.images.renameOnChange.description: When a co-located image's content changes, its content hash in the file name drifts. This controls whether MDForge re-hashes (renames) it and updates the link.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Standard Markdown image link `![](assets/...)` (round-trips with the vault asset scripts).
Obsidian embed `![[assets/...]]` (inserted as literal text; not rendered as an image yet).
mdforge.images.linkStyle.description: How an inserted image is written into the Markdown.

scripts.build: npm run compile:ext && npm run build:webview
